label: context.reference
text:
Slack reaches this task through world_slack. Each Slack message the interface admits arrives as a slack.event artifact with text, user_id, channel_id, thread_ts, message_ts, thread_context and files (small text files carry text_preview). Only members allowed in the Slack application setup are admitted; in channels the bot answers when it is mentioned and then follows that thread.

Reply with artifact.send to world_slack, label slack.operation, payload {"text": "...", "channel": "<channel_id>", "thread_ts": "<thread_ts or message_ts>"}. Use the event's channel_id and its thread_ts; use message_ts to open a thread under a channel message. Without a channel the message goes to the default channel from setup or, when exactly one member is allowed, to that member's direct messages, which is how a task notifies the user on its own initiative. Write Slack markdown; long text is split automatically.

Other effects use {"operation": "<name>", "args": {...}}: message.update and message.delete (channel, ts), reaction.add and reaction.remove (channel, timestamp, name), assistant.status.set (channel, thread_ts, status), and web.call (method, params) for the read methods the interface allows, such as conversations.history, conversations.replies, users.info and users.list.

Each operation answers with slack.delivery.result when Slack accepted it, or world_slack.failure with the reason. A delivery result needs no reply. Report an effect in Slack only after its delivery result arrived.
